dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: Hello there, do you need help? Weren't bowled over by a passing Saurian, were you?

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: Shouldn't happen often, in theory... It's true that some Saurians aren't particularly friendly, but they normally wouldn't attack us unless provoked.

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: But there have been quite a few rumors about Saurians ramming into people near the places where I usually drop off supplies.

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, I work for the Courier's Longhouse, and it's my job to leave regular drops of food and other supplies at the places where our Couriers tend to stop off.

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: Some are for humans, whereas others have been specifically designed for their Saurian companions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They might've been attracted by food.

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: If Saurians or wild animals began to expect food to regularly appear at certain places, it's certainly possible that they'd start hanging around there...

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: And if they were starving, it's not impossible that they might end up charging into people...

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: Thank you for helping me realize what might be going on! I'll have to think of a way of testing this theory out...

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: Hmm... How about this, then? You take these and walk around the wilds a bit more. See if any Saurians crash into— err, I mean, approach you?

dialogues.speaker: Sorimana
dialogues.text: With your skills, you should be able to dodge them, right?
